# Formblatt: Technical Reference and Architecture

Formblatt is a client-side PDF editor and ISO 32000-1 AcroForm compiler. It runs in browser memory using native ES Modules, Mozilla PDF.js, and PDF-Lib.

- Production: https://formblatt.dpdns.org
- Source Code: https://github.com/sshrestha-design/formblatt
- License: MIT

---

## 1. System Architecture

Formblatt operates without backend server dependencies. Document parsing, canvas rendering, field auto-detection, calculation evaluation, and binary PDF assembly run directly in the browser.

### Key Dependencies

- PDF.js: Extracts page dimensions, text content items, font metrics, and renders vector page viewports.
- PDF-Lib: Modifies PDF bytes, constructs AcroForm field dictionaries, generates appearance streams, injects JavaScript calculate actions, and handles PDF flattening.
- ONNX Runtime Web: Runs local neural vision models for form element classification in browser memory.

---

│
├── styles/                     # Modular Stylesheets
│   ├── base.css                # CSS custom properties, resets, and layout grid
│   ├── fonts.css               # WebFont definitions
│   ├── landing.css             # Landing page styles and template cards

    ├── benchmark_speed.js      # Latency and throughput benchmarks
    ├── evaluate_detector_cli.js# Field detection precision and recall benchmark

## 3. Project File Format (`.formblatt` / `.jform`)

Form sessions serialize to JSON:

```json
{
  "version": "1.1.0",
  "appName": "Formblatt",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-21T09:30:00.000Z",
  "fileName": "sample_form.pdf",
  "originalPdfBytes": "<Base64 Encoded PDF Bytes>",
  "fields": [
    {
      "id": "field_1788765432100_1",
      "type": "text",
      "name": "full_name",
      "label": "Full Legal Name",
      "page": 1,
      "x": 72,
      "y": 150,
      "width": 240,
      "height": 28,
      "required": true,
      "readOnly": false,
      "multiline": false,
      "isComb": false,
      "maxLength": null,
      "fontSize": 12,
      "fontFamily": "Helvetica",
      "color": "#0f172a",
      "backgroundColor": "#ffffff",
      "borderColor": "#cbd5e1",
      "borderWidth": 1,
      "borderRadius": 4,
      "alignment": "left",
      "defaultValue": "",
      "placeholder": "e.g. Jane Doe",
      "options": [],
      "calculation": null
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 4. Field Types and PDF Compilation

When exporting interactive PDFs (`js/engines/acroform-builder.js`), fields map to AcroForm specifications:

1. `text`: Single-line or multiline `PDFTextField`. Supports comb character spacing (`isComb`, `maxLen`), text alignment, custom font sizing, and `/AA` calculate action scripts.
2. `staticText`: Non-interactive vector text labels burned directly into the PDF content stream via `page.drawText`.
3. `dropdown`: `PDFDropdown` with selectable options list.
4. `checkbox`: `PDFCheckBox` rendering standard checkmark or cross glyphs.
5. `radio`: `PDFRadioGroup` with grouped option widgets.
6. `signature`: Embeds vector path coordinates, cursive font paths, or PNG/JPEG image stamps.

---

## 5. Calculation Engine

The calculation engine (`js/core/state.js` and `js/engines/acroform-builder.js`) supports:

- Common presets: Sum (`SUM(a, b)`), Product (`PRODUCT(qty, price)`), Tax (`TAX(subtotal, rate)`), and Discount (`DISCOUNT(subtotal, rate)`).
- Custom math expressions: Arithmetic formulas evaluated in topological order.
- PDF-Lib compilation: Compiles JavaScript expressions into ISO-compliant `/AA` calculate actions and registers field calculation order in `/CO` catalog arrays for Adobe Acrobat and web PDF readers.

---

## 6. Field Detection Pipeline

The field detection engine combines three approaches:

1. Native AcroForm Extraction: Reads existing form dictionaries and widget annotations from input PDFs.
2. Vector Geometry Analysis (`js/engines/auto-detector.js`): Scans path drawing operators for horizontal underline strokes, comb boxes, and rectangular boundaries.
3. Optical and Neural Detection (`js/engines/ocr-engine.js` and `js/engines/onnx-detector.js`): Binarizes scanned bitmap pages, extracts contours, and runs local ONNX vision models to detect input boxes and checkboxes.

---

## 7. Development and Testing

```bash
# Start local development server
npm start

# Run 154-test automated regression suite
npm test

# Run throughput and latency benchmarks
npm run bench

# Run field detection precision and recall evaluation
npm run test:detector
```
